prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production character development sheet for PawSync.
Input image 1 is the character design reference. Create a beautiful square 2048x2048 ORIGINAL character sheet for "Maple the Cat" based on the SAME character in the reference. Preserve its species, markings, face, proportions, palette and warm outlined illustration style exactly; do not redesign its identity. Cream paper background, generous spacing, neat small brown rounded typography, thin section dividers. Character system presentation inspired by professional mascot development sheets, no copied brand artwork.
Title "Maple the Cat" at the top, subtitle "PawSync · expressions & interactions".
A clean 3-column by 4-row grid of 12 clearly separated poses with these exact small labels: "Front", "Side", "Back", "Typing", "Wave", "Happy", "Petting", "Sleep", "Surprised", "Drink water", "Stretch", "Reminder".
First row shows consistent front/side/back full-body turnarounds. Other panels show the SAME pet doing the labeled interaction: rounded paw hands tapping cream keyboard, one paw waving, happy smile, eyes closed leaning into a gentle pet, curled asleep with zzz, attentive surprised eyes, sipping from a little water cup, stretching both forepaws up, holding a small reminder bell. Keep the anatomy of a cute animal mascot, rounded mitten paws, no human fingers or human body. Bottom strip separate from grid: modular head, torso, tail, left forepaw and right forepaw, plus close-ups of paws resting, tapping and waving. The paw/hand close-ups must show clear articulation and preserve paw shape across poses.
No duplicate species, no scenery, no extra pets, no watermark. Design consistency, readable labels and animation usefulness matter more than decoration.
